pr_title: Add support for ssh commit signing
pr_body:
Closes #17449

- [x] Verify ssh signatures
- [x] Verification of ssh keys
As we now can add public keys for ssh git commit signing, we also need to be able to verify that the user owns this specific public key, before allowing this for signing verification.
- [x] Added sign/verify tests
To test this you need git 2.34+ and openssh 8.1+
- [x] added some screenshots to show how it looks

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1810977/149632979-f7d4dd4a-aeca-451b-af67-8ae8ea5d3399.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1810977/149633002-bf072dff-d7a0-48d6-897f-edfda772d665.png)
pr_comments: We might want to add some tests to ensure it _works_, I think you can re-cycle some code from the gpg test files.

I can't really reuse any tests from `gpg_key_test.go`. 
I can do a sign and verify tests if you really want, but the library <https://github.com/42wim/sshsig> already does those tests.

> I can do a sign and verify tests if you really want, but the library https://github.com/42wim/sshsig already does those tests.

Could we import those tests? It's mostly beneficial, if someone would touch the verify function the test are in place that it ensures it won't cause a regression in a certain case.

@gusted tests added and merged with current main.
For the tests actually to work, this PR https://gitea.com/gitea/test-env/pulls/12 needs to be merged so we have a `ssh-keygen` that can sign

Thank you for working on this! In my basic tests it seems good.

I don't necessarily want my signing keys to have push access. I may keep separate keys for signing and pushing. Could we have an option to choose whether a given key can push and/or sign?

> Thank you for working on this! In my basic tests it seems good.
> 
> I don't necessarily want my signing keys to have push access. I may keep separate keys for signing and pushing. Could we have an option to choose whether a given key can push and/or sign?

This can be in a follow-up PR
Nice feature 👍, I will leave my L-G-T-M to 1.17 release (1.16 has been frozen)

https://github.com/git/git/pull/1041

### Screenshots

_No response_
comments: Git v2.34.0 is out now with support for this.

Yes, I'm using it.  It's great.  Here's what it looks like currently on github:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/65864/142010765-5f464982-d829-4873-81d7-0aae95f5ad5c.png)

https://github.com/melvincarvalho/melvincarvalho.com/commits/gh-pages

git verify-commit also works

I've mailed github support about changing that from unverified -> verified ... hopefully soon!

If you click on the `unverified` you can see it is recognized as signed, just GitHub doesn't know how to read it. 

>  GitHub supports GPG and S/MIME signatures. We don’t know what type of signature this is. 

See also: https://github.com/github/feedback/discussions/7744

I'm going to try and implement this.
Already created a library to create/verify those armored ssh signatures (https://github.com/42wim/sshsig)

I don't understand what you mean here?
